newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA DEFEND WITH BACKS AGAINST THE WALL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA DEFEND WITH BACKS AGAINST THE WALL.

text.p: South Africa were 30 for no wicket at tea on the fourth day of the first test on Monday still needing 296 to avoid an innings defeat against a record-breaking Australian side.
Not without some alarms Gary Kirsten and Andrew Hudson negotiated the 14 overs bowled to the interval. Kirsten was on eight with Hudson on 30.

Australia finally declared their first innings on 628 for eight, just under an hour after lunch with an overall lead of 326. Steve Waugh and Greg Blewett rewrote the record books with a stand of 385 for the fifth wicket with Waugh making 160 and Blewett 224.
Waugh fell just before lunch and Blewett just after, having hit 34 fours from 421 balls in a marathon stay of eight hours, 39 minutes.

Michael Bevan, the man who had been padded up throughout Blewett's innings, showed that the long wait had not affected his concentration, reaching 37 not out before the declaration arrived with the fall of Shane Warne's wicket, bowled by Hansie Cronje for nine.

Earlier Ian Healy had been brilliantly caught at short midwicket off the spin of Paul Adams for 11. Adams bowled 52 overs and took one for 163. He was one of four South African bowlers who conceded 100 runs.
